reviewed: parts/G_success_criteria_ladder.md and parts/B_research_programme_campaign.md as of 2026-09-23 19:50-19:51 (B6, B7, recomputed Q2/Q5/Q6), plus C.6-C.10, H.5, D.3 and E.2 from CODEX_MASTER_PROMPT.md, 02_RESEARCH_DIRECTIONS.md, 00_README.md, infra/smat_spec.json, infra/myoassist_facts.json and the 2026-09-23 probe. Numbers marked 'scratch Monte Carlo' come from short simulations with assumed variances (the papers report no seed spread); they illustrate orders of magnitude and are not measurements. Items already covered by implementability.json, state_machine_coexistence.json and fidelity_ux.json are referenced, not repeated.

findings.where: Part G.2 L3 (per-seed criteria and ablation directions), G.4 Statistics, G.7 reproduction path ('decisively not reached'); the same per-seed logic in L1 and L2
findings.problem: The L3 verdict is a conjunction of about twenty per-seed and pooled conditions, judged against published values that are single runs with no seed variance. Three structural defects follow. (1) The band is centred on one draw from SMAT's own seed distribution, so even an exact re-implementation has its pooled four-group mean within ±5 pp of 10.1 % with probability only 0.85/0.72/0.61 at n = 3, rising to 0.90/0.79/0.68 as n grows (four-group seed SD 3/4/5 pp); more seeds cannot remove the published draw's own variance. (2) Per-seed conjunctions ('every group reduced on every seed', peak in band per seed, negative power ≤ 15 % per seed, ablation directions per seed) make P(pass) fall as seeds are added, so the gate rewards registering fewer seeds. (3) 'Decisively not reached' (intervals exclude the band) is almost unreachable at n = 3 (t = 4.30) and there is no pre-registered escalation, so the reproduction path mostly returns neither verdict. Scratch Monte Carlo (group SD 2/3/4 pp with inter-group correlation 0.5, peak SD 0.03, negative-power SD 3 pp, 3 % falls per episode, 0.97 per-seed gait pass): P(L3 passes | faithful reconstruction, ablation directions excluded) = 0.69/0.55/0.37 at n = 3 and 0.32/0.21/0.12 at n = 10; with the three ablation directions at 0.95 per seed-criterion, 0.35 (SD 3) and 0.23 (SD 4) at n = 3. UX-06(d) notes that the bands were not derived from seed spread; this finding is about how they are applied.
findings.scenario: A correct reconstruction on 3 seeds fails because gluteus maximus (published −6.6 %) rises 0.4 % on one seed, or one seed's negative-power fraction is 15.3 %. Top-up seeds never gate, so the user registers a 5-seed claim, which is more likely to fail. The programme then reports 'not reproduced' for a faithful implementation, or loops with no verdict. Conversely, a 3-seed pooled mean of 5.2 % with a 95 % interval of 0.1–10.3 % passes as 'reproduced'.
findings.fix: Replace the L3 aggregation now, keeping band centres and widths: '(1) Magnitudes (peak, negative-power fraction, four-group reduction) are judged on the pooled mean: REPRODUCED if it lies in the band; NOT REPRODUCED if its 95 % t-interval lies entirely outside the band with n ≥ 5 and the fidelity checks passed; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. (2) Per seed only catastrophe floors apply, set far outside a faithful seed's spread (peak ≥ 0.5, negative-power fraction ≤ 25 %, fall rate ≤ 30 %); the fraction of seeds inside each band is reported. (3) Directions are pooled: each of the four groups has a one-sided 95 % lower bound above 0 on its pooled reduction. (4) The three ablation directions are three separate claims judged on their seed means, as A2 was published (a mean of three runs); L3-main can pass without them, and each is reported with its own verdict. (5) Every reproduction claim registers a fixed escalation of 3 → 5 → 10 independent pipelines, taken only while the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, with the NOT REPRODUCED test Bonferroni-split over the three looks; these are the claim's top-up seeds. (6) The paper also reports whether each published value lies inside our 95 % prediction interval for one new pipeline (mean ± t·s·√(1 + 1/n)).'
findings.test: gate/tests/test_operating_characteristics.py, frozen with the gate: 2,000 synthetic ledgers per scenario. Faithful (group SD 2 and 3 pp, peak SD 0.03, negative-power SD 3 pp, 3 % falls): P(REPRODUCED at the final look) ≥ 0.8 and non-decreasing across looks. Ablation-like (peak 0.14; or four-group mean 2 %): P(REPRODUCED) ≤ 0.05. Single cases: 3 faithful seeds with glutmax +0.4 % on one seed pass; a 5-seed ledger with pooled mean 1.5 % and interval [0.2, 2.8] is NOT REPRODUCED; the same values at n = 3 are INCONCLUSIVE. The operating-characteristic table is written into docs/paper.

findings.where: Part G.5 (claims), G.8 and D.3 (gate-change), H.5 (add seeds, kill, edit), G.9 (package 'from the best claim'), B.7 Q8
findings.problem: Every protection is per claim, and claims are cheap. (1) After a failed claim, the same hypothesis can be re-registered on fresh seeds. Each claim is valid alone, but k attempts at one-sided α = 0.05 give up to 1 − 0.95^k false passes (10 attempts: 40 %). (2) The registrant chooses 3 or 5 seeds, and with per-seed criteria fewer is easier (RD-01). (3) The Watch panel shows the per-seed numbers, curves and clips of claim arms while they run; an arm that looks bad can be killed and the claim re-registered, and a killed arm has no defined verdict. (4) gate-change may relax a band 'for claims not yet evaluated' after other claims on the same metric have results. That is the post-hoc tolerance change G.0 forbids, moved to the next claim. (5) The eight-week package uses 'the best claim at its current level', which is selection on outcome. (6) Q8's L4 attempts are designed from the Q2–Q6 results and then evaluated on the same S2 blocks (UX-08 covers who registers Q8; this is the leak).
findings.scenario: Claim C1 fails L3 with a pooled four-group reduction of 4.6 %. The user widens the band to ±6 pp through gate-change 'for new claims', with a reason, registers C2 on 3 fresh seeds, gets 5.0 %, and the Watch panel and paper package say 'reproduced'. Every row is in the ledger, but no verdict takes C1 into account.
findings.fix: G.5, add: 'Each claim has family_id = sha256(claim_type, the arm-defining keys of each arm, primary metric, comparator arm). The gate judges families: a superiority or equivalence verdict uses Holm-adjusted α over all claims registered in the family; a reproduction verdict pools the registered seeds of all claims in the family. A killed claim arm, or one paused for more than 14 days, counts as a failed claim with its data so far. A family's seed count and escalation (RD-01) are fixed by its first claim.' G.8 and D.3, replace the gate-change sentence with: 'After the first result on a metric in any claim, a band or threshold on that metric may only be tightened. A relaxation opens an epoch that re-judges every existing claim of the family under both epochs, and both verdicts are printed in the paper.' G.9: replace 'from the best claim' with 'from every claim family at its current level'. B.7 Q8: 'An L4 claim uses S2 blocks whose S1 seeds were drawn after the L4 config was registered.' C.14: the reproducibility statement lists every family, every claim in it and its verdict.
findings.test: Synthetic ledgers: (a) C1 fails, gate-change relaxes, C2 passes: family verdict FAIL, relaxation flagged; (b) ten L4 claims in one family, each at one-sided p = 0.04: FAIL after Holm; (c) SMAT arm killed mid-S4: claim FAIL; (d) a 3-seed claim registered in a family whose first claim fixed 5: rejected at registration; (e) a gate-change that widens a band after any result on its metric: refused.

findings.where: Part G.6 G2, G.7 mechanism path, G.2 L4 last paragraph ('B0-adjusted effect'); B.6 B6 and B7; 02_RESEARCH_DIRECTIONS §6 H-velocity
findings.problem: The mechanism path, described as the almost guaranteed paper, is not machine-decidable and is biased in places. (1) G2 says a control reaching at least half the effect 'is the explanation and moves the claim to the mechanism path', and G.7 applies G2 'as written' to the mechanism path itself: circular. (2) G2 now lists B7, the oracle moment-proportional controller, among the rivals. An oracle is a ceiling, not an explanation. At 25 Nm against a hip moment of roughly 1 Nm/kg it may reach half or more of any learned effect, so every L4 claim, and SMAT itself, would be sent to the mechanism path by a controller that cannot exist on hardware. The same rule treats the baselines B1–B4 and B6 like the confound B0. (3) 'At least half' compares two noisy point estimates as a ratio. (4) The attributions are listed 'for example', and G.7 now accepts any of three (best velocity controller, B6, B0): a union that check_gate.py cannot score. (5) 'The best matched velocity controller' is a maximum over B1, B2 and the B3 member picked after seeing results, which biases toward equivalence. (6) 'The B0-adjusted effect' is undefined. (7) Power (the 5-versus-10 seed conflict itself is IM-20). Scratch Monte Carlo, TOST at ±2 pp, α = 0.05, true difference 0: n = 5 gives power 0.30/0.07 for paired-difference SD 2/3 pp; n = 10 gives 0.80/0.28/0.07 for SD 2/3/4; n = 20 gives 0.99/0.78/0.39. (8) Absence of superiority is not equivalence, but L4 routes 'does not beat B2' straight to 'SMAT's gain is largely velocity control'.
findings.scenario: SMAT − B2 = 1.1 pp with a 90 % interval of [−3.5, 5.7] on 5 blocks. L4 fails, the text routes this to 'largely reward-shaped velocity control', TOST fails, no INCONCLUSIVE outcome exists, and G2 'as written' either refuses the path or loops. Separately, B7 reaches 60 % of a genuinely better learned controller's effect, and G2 moves that method's L4 claim to the mechanism path.
findings.fix: Replace the mechanism-path attributions with computable outcomes on the claim's blocks (block = S2 checkpoint), each a separate pre-declared claim: 'M-reward: the contrast 2·R(B0) − R(SMAT) has a one-sided 95 % lower bound > 0. M-velocity: TOST on R(SMAT) − R(B2) at ±2 pp (α 0.05), with B2 the only primary comparator; B1 and the B3 member are secondary, Holm-adjusted, never best-of. M-simple: the same TOST for B6. M-learned: R(SMAT) − R(B2) and R(SMAT) − R(B6) each have a one-sided 95 % lower bound ≥ 0 and a point estimate ≥ 2 pp. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, reported with the achieved intervals; the words largely velocity control require M-velocity.' Define 'B0-adjusted effect of X = R(X) − R(B0)'; the L4 clause then equals the paired contrast X − SMAT and can be dropped. Split G2 by path: 'Method path: every named rival runs on the claim's blocks, and none of B0, B1–B4 or B6 reaches half of the claim's primary contrast by the linear-contrast test. Mechanism and reproduction paths: completeness only (B0, B2, B4, B6 and A4 on every registered block at matched budgets). B7 is never a rival; it is reported as the fraction of the oracle's reduction achieved.' Equivalence claims use the blinded sample-size re-estimation of RD-18.
findings.test: Synthetic ledgers per outcome (M-reward, M-velocity, M-simple, M-learned, INCONCLUSIVE) each pass alone; a ledger where only the B3 member is within ±2 pp of SMAT must not yield M-velocity; the [−3.5, 5.7] ledger must yield INCONCLUSIVE; a method whose effect B7 reaches at 60 % still passes G2; G2 on a mechanism-path claim checks completeness only.

findings.where: Part B.6 preamble, B0, B1–B4, B6, B7; C.10 'Equal budgets'; E.2 Gate group ('unmatched transitions or torque budget between arms'); smat_spec unspecified choice 16
findings.problem: The decisive controls are not matched in the ways that matter, and the design's own rules would reject them. (1) Torque budget: B.6 requires every arm to use 'the same code, backend class and torque scale', and C.10 defines an equal torque budget as 'the same stage torque scale and command limit'. B0 runs at 0 Nm, so SMAT versus B0 trips the gate's 'unmatched torque budget' violation, and every B0 comparison becomes 'not comparable'. (2) Stages: SMAT runs S3 (1.1 M transitions, human frozen, critic updated on the new reward) and then S4 (66 M). B0, B1–B4, B6 and B7 run S4 only, so per-stage transitions differ (C.10 requires equality per stage), and only SMAT's critic has seen the new reward before S4. (3) Reward channel: under the default team reward (one advantage on the summed reward), SMAT's human is paid 4.0·dt·0.3·u·ω̂ for fast hip motion in phase with the torque. The prompt does not say whether the fixed-controller arms' humans receive r_exo4 and r_Δτ at the controller's command ('the Stage-4 human reward'). (4) The +2 human input layer: B0's human must see the applied command (0), with the same input-growth initialisation, not an unapplied actor output. (5) S4 hyper-parameters (entropy 0.003, lr 3e-5, optimiser and normaliser rules) are not stated for the control arms. (6) Dose: B2, B6 and B7 are set to SMAT's torque limit, not to its delivered positive work, so SMAT > B2 can mean more work rather than better timing.
findings.scenario: B2's human is trained without r_exo4 while SMAT's human is paid for hip velocity × u. SMAT walks with a larger hip range of motion and lower hip activation, and the difference is written up as 'learned co-adaptation'. Or check_gate.py rejects every B0 row as unmatched in torque, and the mechanism path never completes.
findings.fix: B.6, add: 'Reward matching: every arm's human is trained on the same scalar reward function of (state, applied command) as SMAT's human, including r_exo4 and r_Δτ evaluated at the applied command (identically 0 for B0), with the same reward-to-actor assignment and critic form. A two-head-critic sensitivity reruns SMAT and B2 with the exo terms removed from the human's advantage. Stage matching: B0, B1–B4, B6 and B7 run an S3-equivalent of 1.1 M transitions (human frozen, Stage-3 human reward, the arm's own command: 0 for B0, the fixed law at 6 Nm for the controllers), updating the critic only, then S4 for 66 M with SMAT's S4 hyper-parameters, optimiser and normaliser rules and the same +2 input growth, with the human observing the applied command. Dose: report RMS torque and positive work for every arm, and add B2-w, whose gain is set on tuning blocks so that its median positive work matches SMAT's.' C.10, add: 'Torque-budget equality applies among assisted arms. Declared contrast arms (B0, A1–A4) are exempt for the manipulated variable only, and the claim lists them.'
findings.test: Synthetic ledgers: SMAT versus B0 with the exemption declared is comparable; SMAT versus B2 where B2's human reward hash differs from SMAT's is 'not comparable'; B0 without the S3-equivalent is 'not comparable'; an arm without RMS-torque and positive-work fields cannot enter a claim.

findings.where: Part G.2 L5 (assistance and replication gates); B.8 human route (b) and the matched matrix (C1, C2); E.4 M1 ('gate/ complete for every path, then freeze gate/')
findings.problem: (1) The assistance gate compares the assisted condition with 'the same human wearing the passive device'. The assisted human is co-adapted with the device for extra transitions; the passive-device human is not required to receive the same training budget, reward and schedule. That is the confound B0 exists to remove, reintroduced at L5. (2) Route (b), direct-excitation imitation of sprint data, tracks a time-indexed reference, so its speed and 200 m time are set by the data. The replication gate is then met by construction, and assistance cannot shorten the time unless the reward pays for exceeding the reference, which 'published reward unchanged' forbids. Because gate/ freezes in M1 for every path, these texts will be frozen long before Phase 2 is built (IM-13 covers the epoch mechanics).
findings.scenario: The assisted human trains 200 M more transitions than the passive-device human and runs 0.6 s faster over 200 m; the gate passes and a sprint gain is claimed. A matched continuation of the passive-device human would have gained the same 0.6 s.
findings.fix: L5, replace the comparator: 'assistance gate: ... versus C1-matched: the same parent human wearing the device at zero torque and continued for exactly the transitions, reward and stage schedule of the assisted condition's co-adaptation (the Phase-2 B0); the comparison with the un-continued passive human is reported beside it.' B.8 route (b): 'counts toward L5 only with a speed-maximising task reward in which imitation is a style term; that reward is pre-registered and frozen before the route's first run, and the replication gate's published-reward clause then refers to it.' Freeze L5 in its own gate epoch when Phase 2 is built, not in M1.
findings.test: Synthetic sprint ledgers: a passive comparator with fewer transitions than the assisted arm is refused; a route-(b) human with a pure time-indexed imitation reward is excluded from L5; C1-matched with equal budgets is comparable.

findings.where: Part B.6 'How the simple arms are tuned', B3, B6, B7; G.2 L4 ('beats B2, B4 and B6')
findings.problem: Tuning effort and tuning conditions are asymmetric in SMAT's favour. SMAT's exo actor gets 67 M transitions of closed-loop optimisation with the adapting human. Each simple family gets a small grid screened on the frozen S2 human (evaluation only), and the member chosen there is the only one that co-adapts. The best member for a non-adapted human need not be the best after 66 M of co-adaptation: for a delayed-feedback law, gain and delay interact with the human's adapted timing. The screening metric is not named, and the text does not require the screening blocks to be disjoint from the claim's S2 blocks (the seed-pool side of this is UX-07 and IM-10).
findings.scenario: B6's κ and Δ, chosen on the frozen human, favour a large κ; after co-adaptation, a smaller κ with a longer Δ would have reduced activation more. SMAT beats the mistuned B6 by 2.4 pp, and L4 records 'better than a published controller'. A reviewer who re-tunes B6 in closed loop cannot reproduce the gap.
findings.fix: B.6, replace the tuning paragraph: 'Each family (B3, B6, B7, and B4's amplitude) is tuned on at least 3 tuning blocks (S2 checkpoints from training seeds never used by a claim) with a declared metric (the four-group reduction on selection seeds). The grid is screened on the frozen S2 human; the top 3 members then co-adapt for 20 M transitions on the tuning blocks; the rule picks the member with the largest co-adapted reduction; only that member runs the 66 M on the claim blocks. Each arm's tuning budget (grid points × transitions) is reported beside SMAT's 67 M of exo optimisation, and the second-best member is a reported sensitivity row.'
findings.test: Synthetic ledgers: a B6 member selected using a claim block makes the claim refused; an L4 card without the tuning-budget field is refused by the validator; every family has its 20 M co-adapted tuning step before its 66 M arm starts.

findings.where: Part B.3 rank 4 (step counting); B.7 Q4, Q5, Q6 and Q7; G.2 L3 ablation directions; smat_spec ppo_by_stage.derived_updates_per_stage
findings.problem: Under the default aggregate reading, Stage 3 is 1.1 M transitions: 16.8 PPO updates, about 1,344 minibatch steps at lr 3e-5, each update cut short by target KL 0.01. The exo actor will barely move from its initialisation, so full SMAT's Stage 4 starts from a nearly untrained exo actor. That is close to A2 ('Stage 4 only' with a random exo actor), the arm the gate requires to collapse (peak ≤ 0.30) while SMAT must reach 0.83. A1 (bang-bang for at least 50 % of the cycle after S3) is also unlikely at 16.8 updates. The per-environment reading (537 updates, about 30 CPU-minutes per S3) is scheduled in Q7, after Q4–Q6. Choosing the reading afterwards by which one reproduces L3 would be tuning to the published number. Whether 16.8 updates suffice cannot be checked without running it: the risk is plausible, not proven.
findings.scenario: Q4 fails L3 because SMAT and A2 look alike. Most of the 4.7 B transitions of Q5 and Q6 were spent on that reading, and their S3–S4 arms must be rerun after Q7; the switch is then justified by the L3 outcome.
findings.fix: Move into Q4, before any S4 job: 'S3 reading selection: on each S2 block, run S3 at 1.1 M (aggregate) and at 35 M (per environment) with the frozen S2 human. Select by a known-answer criterion that uses no L3 metric: the S3 exo actor's executed command satisfies |u| ≥ 0.95 with sign(u) = sign(ω) on at least 50 % of gait-cycle samples at 6 Nm, the optimum of r_exo3. If both or neither pass, keep the aggregate reading and report it.' Add: 'If the per-environment reading is also used for S4 (2.1 B transitions per arm), every arm of every block runs at that S4 budget on one backend. On the CPU this is infeasible (about 12 arms × 10 blocks = 253 B transitions, ~147 days at 20k/s), so S4 then stays at 66 M and this is reported.' L4(b): 'SMAT's total transitions are those of the reproduced SMAT arm under the reading used in the claim.'
findings.test: Synthetic ledgers: an S3 reading selected after an L3 result exists is flagged 'selected on outcome'; a SMAT arm at the per-environment S4 budget compared with B2 at the aggregate budget is 'not comparable'; the Q4 catalogue contains both S3 readings before its S4 entries.

findings.where: Part B.2 'Trainer and stages' ('per-actor log-std parameters (never a shared vector)'); B.3 ranks 1–3 and 15; C.8; myoassist_facts.json action_mapping, separated_networks, training_mechanics
findings.problem: The registry defaults are good practice, but unlike SMAT's probable implementation. MyoAssist, which SMAT used, has a Tanh mean head with unsquashed Gaussian noise clipped to [−1, 1] by SB3 (the registry's 'clipped Gaussian', not its tanh-squashed default); no observation normalisation (default: running mean/std); one joint PPO ratio and one shared target-KL stop over all 28 action dimensions (default: per-actor ratios); one log-std Parameter spanning both actors, so a 'frozen' actor's noise keeps training (forbidden outright); and orthogonal gain 1 on every layer including the outputs (not a registry option). Q2 selects the Stage-1 config by L1, so it may carry forward a config unlike SMAT's. Two consequences. First, the activation regime: the Fig. 4 read in smat_spec shows rectus femoris and iliopsoas near activation 1.0 for much of the cycle, consistent with clipped-Gaussian saturation, and relative reductions from a saturated baseline differ from those of an unsaturated one for reasons unrelated to the mechanism. Second, the published A2 collapse, which contradicts the reward algebra, has its most plausible causes in exactly these era defects (large random exo outputs under β·u² and the rate penalty; noise drift in the 'frozen' human), and the design makes them untestable.
findings.scenario: The engineered reconstruction learns u ≈ ω̂ in A2 (no collapse) and shows a 20 % four-group reduction from an unsaturated baseline. L3 fails, and the paper says 'SMAT does not reproduce' when the gap is an implementation-era effect nobody tested.
findings.fix: B.7, add to Q3–Q5 a pre-registered era-faithful pipeline, carried to L3 whenever it passes L1, whatever its Q2 rank: 'clipped Gaussian with a Tanh mean head, log-std init 0.0 (and −2.0 as a second arm), no observation normalisation, one joint ratio with a shared target-KL stop, one log-std Parameter spanning both actors with the frozen actor's entries left in the optimiser, orthogonal gain 1 on every layer, 1/1200 s physics, and the target-speed bug off and on.' B.2: change 'never a shared vector' to 'never by default; only in the era-faithful arm'. Report era-faithful and engineered reproductions side by side; a divergence between them is a result. L2 report: absolute S2 activation per group and the fraction of time above 0.95, beside the Fig. 4 read.
findings.test: The config schema accepts a shared log-std only with purpose era_faithful; the freeze-hash test expects the human's log-std entries to change during S3 for that arm and for no other; a campaign test asserts that the era-faithful pipeline reaches Q4 whenever its L1 claim passes.

findings.where: Part B.7 Q2 (selection rule, P3 'fresh seeds', miss check); C.7 (successive halving, calibrated tiers); G.5 (claim created 'when a candidate first meets L1'). Budget and seed-pool aspects are IM-09, IM-10 and UX-07.
findings.problem: (1) The 'P3 on 3 fresh seeds' are used both to choose among the three finalists and as the L1 claim's seeds and the parents of every later stage: winner's curse on L1 and on the whole lineage. (2) A claim is created when a candidate first meets L1, that is, after its own result. (3) The lexicographic rule 'L1 pass count, then symmetry deficit, then speed error' is undefined where it matters. At P1 (40 M, an eighth of Stage 1) almost no member passes, symmetry and toe-off need valid gait cycles, and 'pass count' is not defined (seeds or criteria). There is no scalar for the calibration's Spearman ρ. (4) The calibration's pass rule has little power. With 8 configurations, a scratch Monte Carlo (bivariate normal, percentile bootstrap of Spearman ρ) gives P(lower bound > 0.3) = 0.25 at true correlation 0.8, 0.46 at 0.9 and 0.69 at 0.95, so P1 is almost never trusted. (5) The miss check (3 configs × 1 seed) has no decision rule. (6) 24 random draws over about 2,900 combinations are unbalanced, and value normalisation, a leading on-policy sensitivity, is not in the Stage-1 sweep.
findings.scenario: The three finalists pass L1 on 2/3, 3/3 and 2/3 seeds; the 3/3 member is chosen, and its seeds become the L1 claim and the L3 lineage. On new seeds it passes 2/3: the 'L1 met' was selection noise, and L2 and L3 inherit unusually good Stage-1 policies.
findings.fix: B.7 Q2 and C.7, replace the selection rule: 'Screening score, defined for every policy: the mean over L1 criteria of the normalised distance to the band (0 inside), with undefined gait metrics set to the worst value and falls counted. Members within 3 standard errors of the noise floor are tied and all kept, up to the cap. Exactly one config is selected at P3 on the selection seeds. Its L1 claim is then registered, before its seeds run, on 3 confirmation seeds never used before; only confirmation seeds count toward L1 and parent S2. If confirmation fails, the next-ranked config gets its own confirmation, and the number of confirmations is reported.' G.5: 'A claim is registered before any of its seeds' first job.' Replace the random design by a balanced mixed-level orthogonal array of 24 runs, and add value normalisation. Calibration: 'trust P1 if the top-third recall is ≥ 0.6 on at least 12 configurations', otherwise fall back to P2 by default. Miss check: 'a non-promoted config that passes L1 on its seed enters confirmation, and Stage-1 P1 is marked miscalibrated.'
findings.test: Synthetic sweep ledgers: an L1 claim whose seeds took part in selection stays 'screening'; a claim created after its seeds' results is rejected; ranking 24 all-failing P1 members is deterministic and uses the score, not ties; a passing miss-check member triggers confirmation.

findings.where: Part G.3 'Activation reductions'; G.2 L1 speed band and L3 'gait preserved'
findings.problem: Stage 2 and Stage 4 may each walk anywhere in 1.25 ± 0.10 m/s, and Stage 4 weights speed 1.5 against 0.8. Hip-muscle activation rises with walking speed, so a within-seed S2–S4 speed difference of 0.1–0.2 m/s can move a group's time-averaged activation by an amount comparable to the ±5 pp band (the size of this slope in myolegs26 was not checked here and should be measured). Time-averaged activation also changes with cadence at a fixed speed. The relative reduction depends on the baseline level too: near-saturated baselines (the Fig. 4 read) compress it, and low baselines inflate it.
findings.scenario: S4 walks 0.12 m/s slower than S2 on each seed; activation falls 9 % from speed alone; L3 passes. The speed difference appears nowhere in the gate.
findings.fix: G.3, add: 'Co-primary reduction per metre: per group, the time integral of activation divided by the distance walked, computed per cycle and averaged; the time-averaged reduction is reported beside it. Report per seed v_X − v_S2 and cadence for every arm.' L3 gait-preserved: '|v_S4 − v_S2| ≤ 0.05 m/s per seed'. L2 report: absolute S2 activation per group and the fraction of time above 0.95. In Q1, measure the activation-speed slope of the first walking checkpoint at target speeds of 1.15, 1.25 and 1.35 m/s.
findings.test: Synthetic rollouts in which S4 has the same per-stride activation at every speed but walks 0.15 m/s slower: the per-metre reduction is 0 within noise, the time-averaged one is not, and the gait-preserved check fails.

findings.where: Part G.4 first paragraph ('four-group reduction 10.1 % versus 0 for no assistance'); G.2 L3 report line; C.12 card validator and ladder words
findings.problem: G.4 says the bands stay inside the distance between SMAT and its nearest ablation, including 'four-group reduction 10.1 % versus 0 for no assistance'. That 0 was never measured. For this metric the nearest rival is B0, the reward change alone (effort weight ×15 and a squared penalty on exactly these four muscles), whose reduction may itself fall inside 5.1–15.1 %. A reconstruction whose torque contributes nothing then passes the activation criterion, and L3 prints 'reproduced' while B0 is only 'reported beside' and may not have run yet.
findings.scenario: SMAT 9.8 % and B0 9.1 % on the same blocks: L3 passes, and the card reads 'reproduced: 9.8 % (published 10.1 %)'.
findings.fix: G.4: delete '10.1 % versus 0 for no assistance' and add: 'For the activation metric the band tests fidelity to the published number only. The device-attributable reduction R(SMAT) − R(B0), with its paired interval, is printed on the same line.' C.12: 'The validator refuses the word reproduced for an activation number unless B0 exists on the same blocks, and prints reproduced (of which reward-only: X pp).'
findings.test: Card-validator tests: an L3 activation card without B0 on the same blocks is refused; with B0, the extra line is present and equals the ledger.

findings.where: Part G.3 'Normalised peak torque' and 'Negative-power time fraction'; G.2 L3 bands and ablation thresholds; smat_spec evaluation_metrics (ambiguities)
findings.problem: The published 0.83 is read from the bilateral mean profile (O Fig. 3c), and the 10 % 'fraction of the gait cycle where P < 0' from the mean power profile (Fig. 3d); smat_spec lists both ambiguities. G.3 instead uses the mean of per-cycle peaks, which is never below the peak of the mean, and the pooled fraction of control steps, which cycle-to-cycle jitter around the zero crossings inflates. There is no deadband, so near-zero torques with noise count as negative power, and that decides the A2 and A3 thresholds (≥ 20 %, ≥ 25 %).
findings.scenario: SMAT's mean profile has 10 % negative time, but zero crossings jitter by ±2 control steps, so the pooled per-step fraction is 16 %: L3 fails on negative power for a faithful controller.
findings.fix: G.3: 'Normalised peak torque (primary): the maximum of the gait-cycle-normalised mean |u| profile per side, averaged over sides; secondary: the mean of per-cycle peaks. Negative-power time fraction (primary): the fraction of the 101 samples of the gait-cycle-normalised mean power profile with P < −P0, per side, averaged over sides; secondary: the pooled per-step fraction. P0 = 0.5 W. The ablation directions use the primary definitions.' Freeze P0 with the gate.
findings.test: Synthetic traces with a known mean-profile negative fraction of 10 % and ±2-step jitter: primary 10 %, secondary above 10 %; a zero-torque trace with 1e-6 Nm noise: 0 % negative.

findings.where: Part G.4 precision rule ('a quarter of the band's half-width'); G.2 L1 and L3 fall-rate and direction criteria; G.3 gait events. The mechanism and timing of the precision rule are IM-09 and IM-11; the definition of a fall is IM-21.
findings.problem: (1) 'Half-width' is undefined for the one-sided and binary criteria that carry the most per-seed risk: symmetry ≥ 0.92, RMSE ≤ 3.6°, negative power ≤ 15 %, falls ≤ 10 %, and 'every group reduced'. (2) With E = 20 the fall rate is binomial: a true 5 % rate fails '≤ 10 %' on a seed with P = 0.075 (21 % over 3 seeds, 32 % over 5); a true 8 % rate fails with P = 0.21 per seed (51 % over 3). (3) Cycles just before a fall are kept, which biases metrics toward abnormal cycles, and a high rejected-cycle count never invalidates a metric.
findings.scenario: A policy with a true 5 % fall rate fails L1 on one of three seeds because 3 of 20 episodes fell. The precision rule never triggers, because the fall criterion has no half-width.
findings.fix: G.4: 'For one-sided criteria the operational half-width h is |published value − threshold| where a published value exists (negative power: 5 pp), otherwise declared now in criteria.yaml (symmetry r: 0.04; RMSE: 1.0°; direction criteria: 2 pp). The fall rate uses at least 100 episodes and passes if the point estimate is ≤ 10 % and the exact one-sided 95 % upper bound is ≤ 15 %.' G.3: 'Cycles that end within 1 s before a fall are excluded; a metric is invalid, and the seed fails that criterion, if more than 20 % of detected cycles are rejected.'
findings.test: Simulate 2,000 seeds with a true 5 % fall rate under the new rule: per-seed false failure ≤ 5 %; synthetic rollouts with 30 % rejected cycles make the gait metrics invalid.

findings.where: Part B.6 'Positive controls' (P1–P3); 02_RESEARCH_DIRECTIONS §5 and §8 (the planned 'Stage 1 does not reproduce' verdict)
findings.problem: P1 runs a different model (22-muscle, planar), reward and device, with no pass criterion ('walk stably'), so it cannot tell a walk26 bug from a model limit. P2 ('B2 lowers hip activation relative to zero torque on the frozen S2 human; a direction that follows from physics') is not a known answer: a frozen policy's excitations are state feedback trained with hip imitation on, and an external flexion torque can raise tracking or antagonist activity. P2 can fail on a correct implementation and block every negative verdict, or pass on a broken one. P3 (L0–L2 must pass) makes 'Stage 1 does not reproduce' impossible to report, although 02 §5 and §8 plan that verdict.
findings.scenario: The 3D reconstruction cannot reach L1 after the Q2 extension. P3 fails by definition, and the only allowed wording is 'not yet tested', indefinitely.
findings.fix: Replace P1–P3 with known-answer controls that have numeric pass rules: 'K-exo3: the S3 exo actor on the frozen S2 human reaches the r_exo3 optimum (|u| ≥ 0.95 with sign(u) = sign(ω) on ≥ 50 % of samples). K-exo4: an exo actor trained on r_exo4 + r_Δτ alone against the frozen S2 human reaches R² ≥ 0.9 against the filtered velocity law. K-effort: B0 lowers the four-group mean activation below S2 (the ×15 effort gradient). K-env: MyoAssist's own trainer and ours, on the same composed model at P2 on 2 seeds, both meet the L1 speed and fall-rate criteria, or both fail. K-metric: eval/core recovers an injected 10.0 % activation change within ±0.2 pp from synthetic rollouts.' Verdicts by stage: 'A Stage-1 non-reproduction needs K-env and K-metric; a Stage-4 non-reproduction needs K-exo3, K-exo4, K-effort, K-metric and L0–L2.'
findings.test: Synthetic ledgers: a Stage-1 failure with K-env and K-metric passing allows 'Stage 1 does not reproduce under documented choices'; a Stage-4 failure with K-exo4 failing gives 'not yet tested'.

findings.where: Part G.1 fourth bullet; B.6 B1–B3; G.2 L3 report ('fraction of SMAT's command variance explained'); 02_RESEARCH_DIRECTIONS §0 and §6; smat_spec derived_analysis.rate_penalty_filter
findings.problem: B2's filter is the discounted LQ optimum of the exo reward terms alone, derived with ω̂ held constant (smat_spec). For a periodic ω̂, the exo actor, which sees q and q̇ at t, t−1 and t−2, can extrapolate and lead the velocity; under the team reward it is also paid through the human terms. So SMAT > B2 may only mean 'a better linear filter', not co-adaptation. And SMAT ≈ B2, or a high share of command variance explained, shows similar outcomes or behaviour, not that the learned controller is velocity control. A reviewer will also note that r_exo4 was designed to reward positive power, so recovering its optimum confirms that the reward works rather than refuting the method.
findings.scenario: SMAT beats B2 by 2.5 pp and the paper claims that learned co-adaptation matters; a closed-form predictor-corrected filter on the same 18 inputs would have matched SMAT.
findings.fix: B.6, add: 'B2+: the LQ tracker of r_exo4 + r_Δτ with a one-step linear predictor of ω̂ from the same three samples (closed form, no learning). B8: the best linear policy on the exo actor's 18 inputs, fitted by least squares to SMAT's S4 commands on tuning blocks and frozen before the claim blocks (tests whether nonlinearity matters).' G.7 and 02 §6: 'M-velocity is worded as a matched closed-form controller, with the human co-adapted at the same budget, achieves an equivalent reduction, never as SMAT is velocity control. M-learned requires SMAT to beat B2, B2+ and B8.'
findings.test: Synthetic ledger where SMAT beats B2 but not B2+: M-learned refused. Unit test: on a sinusoidal ω̂, B2+ earns more r_exo4 + r_Δτ than B2.

findings.where: Part G.2 L4(c); G.5 partner seeds; B.6 cross-play ('The fixed laws (B2, B6) have nothing to overfit'); G.6 G4; 02 §6 H-partner. The partner-training budget is IM-22.
findings.problem: (1) The held-out S4 humans were co-adapted to SMAT devices, so SMAT-like devices meet familiar partners while B2 and B6 meet unfamiliar ones. S4 humans also carry the +2 command inputs trained on another device's command statistics: a distribution shift, not partner transfer. (2) The comparator for a cross-play reduction is undefined (the partner's own S2? its S4 with its own device?). (3) Retention = cross/self is a ratio of noisy quantities 'with an interval above zero', and 'retention exceeds SMAT's by 0.10' compares two ratios; G4's 'at least 50 % ... with an interval above zero' has the same problem. (4) Matrix cells share devices and humans (crossed random effects), so a naive interval over cells is pseudo-replicated. (5) 'The fixed laws have nothing to overfit' is wrong: B2's and B6's humans co-adapted to them, so their self-play-to-cross-play gap measures human-side specialisation, and B.6 now uses that gap as the no-overfitting calibration.
findings.scenario: SMAT retention 0.85 against a partner-robust method's 0.97 on a 5 × 5 matrix; a naive t-interval over 25 cells is narrow and L4(c) passes. The difference comes from the partner pool being SMAT-adapted.
findings.fix: G.2 L4(c) and B.6: 'Primary partners are device-naive S2 humans from at least 5 held-out pipelines. Secondary partners are S4 humans balanced across arms, so that each arm's device meets humans adapted to every arm's device equally often. The cross-play reduction of device d with partner h is h's activation with d, no adaptation, relative to h at zero torque on the same evaluation seeds. Retention is tested as the linear contrast cross − 0.7·self > 0, and differences between arms with a crossed random-effects model (device and human random) or a two-way bootstrap over devices and humans. Device-side overfitting is the device × partner-origin interaction in a 2 × 2 of (SMAT, B2) devices by (SMAT-adapted, B2-adapted) humans, not B2's gap alone.' Apply the same linear-contrast form to G4.
findings.test: A synthetic matrix with a human-only main effect and no interaction shows no retention difference between arms; check_gate refuses a naive per-cell interval; the 2 × 2 interaction recovers an injected device-side overfit.

findings.where: Part B.5 gates 3–5 and the certificate; B.7 Q7 ('S4 only on the certified GPU backend') and Q8; C.9; probe parity (6 versus 10 contacts at the same seated state; contact counts differ in 84 % of steps)
findings.problem: (1) Learning parity covers Stage 1 only, on 3 seeds, with margins equal to the full L1 bands (lenient), while the GPU is meant for S3–S4 work (Q7, Q8), where the headline metric lives. (2) The registered GPU geometry (4,096 worlds × 16 steps) truncates GAE at 16 steps instead of SMAT's 2,048: an algorithmic change that Stage-1 parity does not certify for S4, whose rewards act on fast time scales. (3) Statistical parity uses one policy, and its margin ('a quarter of that metric's band half-width') is undefined for several listed metrics: per-group mean activation, contact counts, peak ground-reaction force and fall rate. (4) The probe found systematic contact differences, not only chaos. A GPU-trained policy that exploits them is penalised on CPU evaluation, possibly unequally across arms (a learned exo actor more than a fixed law). (5) MULTICCD is off everywhere and changes CPU contacts in 30–42 % of steps, so our physics also differ from SMAT-era defaults.
findings.scenario: The certificate is issued on Stage-1 parity, and per-environment S4 runs on the GPU for SMAT and B0. The GPU-trained SMAT loses 3 pp on CPU evaluation relative to its CPU-trained twin, B0 loses nothing, and the mechanism contrast shifts by 3 pp.
findings.fix: B.5, add gate 4b: 'S3–S4 learning parity: from the same CPU-trained S2 checkpoints (at least 5 blocks), SMAT and B0 are trained on both backends in the registered GPU geometry and evaluated on the CPU; TOST on each L3 metric and on the SMAT − B0 contrast, with margins of half the L3 band half-widths. Without 4b the GPU serves Stages 1–2 and screening only.' Gate 3: 'at least 3 policies (S1, S4 and B2), with margins declared now for every listed metric (per-group activation: 2 % of the CPU mean; contact count: 0.5 per step; peak GRF: 5 % of body weight; fall rate: 3 points).' Add a one-checkpoint CPU sensitivity (MULTICCD default versus disabled) on the L1 metrics, reported as a model limitation.
findings.test: A synthetic parity report without 4b: the certificate is refused for S3–S4 job kinds. A parity report missing a margin for any listed metric fails certification.

findings.where: Part B.6 (paired arms, one S4 run per arm per block); G.2 L3 and L4 seed counts; C.6 paired blocks; README seeds row
findings.problem: The only replicate unit is an independent full pipeline (about 0.55 B transitions). The mechanism contrasts need about 10–20 blocks for TOST at ±2 pp (RD-03), which costs about 3–8 B transitions of new pipelines before any control runs. Much of the variance of a paired S4 contrast may come from S4 training noise, which cheap 66 M replicates within a block can reduce, rather than from the S2 human, which only new pipelines can reduce. The design has no variance decomposition and no rule for replicates, and adding S4 replicates naively as seeds would be pseudo-replication.
findings.scenario: Reaching 10 independent pipelines with controls takes about 6 B transitions (IM-20 proposes the block). Adding two S4 replicates of SMAT and B2 on the 5 existing blocks would cost about 1.3 B and might reach the same precision for the primary contrast, or might not. Nobody knows, because the variance components were never estimated.
findings.fix: B.6 and G.4, add: 'Mechanism contrasts use b blocks (S2 checkpoints of independent S1–S2 seeds) × r S4 replicates per arm with distinct S3–S4 seeds. Replicates are averaged within a block and the block is the unit (df = b − 1), or a mixed model with block as a random effect is used. (b, r) is chosen from a blinded variance-decomposition pilot on the first 3 blocks with r = 2 for SMAT and B2 (only variances are computed; no contrast is shown), with b ≥ 5 always. Equivalence claims use one blinded sample-size re-estimation after 5 blocks, capped at 20. L3 keeps independent full pipelines for the reproduction verdict.'
findings.test: A synthetic ledger with r = 3 replicates on 3 blocks reports df = 2, not 8; the blinded pilot writes only variance components to the ledger.

findings.where: Part B.7 table (Q5, Q6, Q7); G.6 G2 (K1–K3); B.6 B5 and critic variants
findings.problem: The pre-loaded campaign cannot complete any path's G2. G2 requires K1–K3 (frozen-then-joint, progressive versus final reward, progressive versus final torque), and B5 isolates staging from initialisation, but Q5 queues K1 only; K2, K3, B5 and the critic variants are in no block. After about 14 B transitions (Q2–Q6) the paper gate therefore waits on user action. The per-environment S4 reading (Q7) is also unbudgeted for the controls: if it is the reading used, every arm needs 2.1 B transitions per block (RD-07).
findings.scenario: Q6 finishes; L3 and the controls look clean; the paper gate reports 'G2: K2, K3 missing'. The user must register them by hand, and they queue behind whatever else has been added.
findings.fix: B.7, add a pre-registered block after Q5: 'Q5b Schedule contrasts: K2, K3 and B5 (with and without the behaviour-cloned warm start) on the same blocks, 67 M each (about 0.8 B on 3 blocks, 1.3 B on 5), plus the critic-variant arm.' Add a test that derives each paper path's required arms from gate/criteria.yaml and asserts that every one is in some pre-registered block.
findings.test: tests/test_campaign_covers_gate.py: for each path of G.7, the arms its G1 and G2 require appear in campaign.yaml with matching budgets. It fails today on K2, K3 and B5.

findings.where: Part G.2 L5 (replication gate, assistance-gate statistics, architecture gate, realistic actuator); G.3 sprint metrics; B.8 (the device, the task, 'beside Moon et al.'s human effect')
findings.problem: (1) Maximum speed is the peak 0.5 s moving average over any run, including failed runs, so a forward lunge or fall can reach 4.0 m/s. (2) 4.0 m/s is fast running, not sprinting, and without fatigue a 200 m time is acceleration plus top speed; calling the result 'sprint-time reduction' will not survive a biomechanics reviewer unless the human sprints. (3) 'Beats, or explains the failure of' in the architecture gate cannot fail, and 'beats' has no test. (4) Unknown actuator parameters are 'swept and labelled' (the Moon digest is marked PARTIAL, with its mechanism and protocol pending), so 'the gain survives the realistic actuator' can be met at the most favourable swept point. (5) A bootstrap over 5 seeds and paired starts under-covers and treats starts within a seed as independent; the unit of the median (episodes or seed medians) is unstated. (6) Reporting simulated seconds beside Moon et al.'s 0.97 s mixes a run of about 50 s at 4 m/s with human runs of about 30 s; percentages are comparable, seconds are not.
findings.scenario: The cable model's delay and power envelope are swept. At the least restrictive corner the gain is 0.55 s and L5 passes there, while the nominal parameters give 0.2 s.
findings.fix: L5: 'Maximum speed counts only completed runs, sustained over a flying 20 m segment. The endpoint is named fast-running 200 m time unless the unassisted human sustains at least 6 m/s. Architecture gate: C6 − C3 and C6 − C5, each by a one-sided paired test at a 0.5 s margin; delete or explains the failure of. Realistic actuator: a nominal parameter set pre-registered from the literature before the first Phase-2 run; the gain must hold at the nominal point and at a pre-registered pessimistic corner, and the sweep is sensitivity only. Statistics: the seed is the unit (per-seed mean time over starts, failures ranked last), with a paired t or permutation test over at least 5 seeds; effects are reported in seconds and in percent of each condition's own time.'
findings.test: Synthetic sprint ledgers: a replication gate met only by failed runs fails; an actuator result that passes only at a swept corner is labelled ideal-actuator, not L5; the architecture gate with C6 no better than C3 fails.

findings.where: Part G.2 L4 ('at least one of (a), (b), (c)'; '95 % interval ... above zero'); G.4 ('one-sided 95 % bound'); G.7 (three alternative attributions); G.2 L3 report list
findings.problem: Conjunctions are handled correctly (an intersection-union test needs no adjustment), but disjunctions are not. L4 passes on any of (a), (b) or (c), and the mechanism path on any of three attributions, so the error rate can reach three times the nominal. About twenty secondary contrasts (B0–B7, A1–A4, K1–K3, critic variants, six-group, offline replay) are reported at a nominal 95 % with no family-wise label. The level also differs: G.4 says superiority uses the one-sided 95 % bound, while L4 asks for a 95 % interval above zero (one-sided 97.5 %).
findings.scenario: A method's (a), (b) and (c) claims each reach one-sided p ≈ 0.04; one passes by chance and L4 is met. The paper also lists two 'significant' secondary contrasts out of twenty, about what chance alone produces.
findings.fix: G.2 L4: 'A method registers one primary sub-criterion; any further sub-criteria of the same method are tested with Holm's step-down procedure at family α = 0.05.' G.7: the attributions are separate claims under RD-03, Holm-adjusted within the family. G.4: 'Superiority uses the one-sided 95 % lower bound of the paired difference everywhere (L4, G1, G2, G4); every secondary contrast in a paper table carries a Holm-adjusted p-value or the label exploratory.'
findings.test: Synthetic ledger with three L4 sub-claims each at one-sided p = 0.04: fails after Holm; with one at p = 0.01: passes. A unit test on a fixed ledger shows that L4 and G.4 use the same bound.

findings.where: Part C.10 'Equal budgets', C.6 paired blocks, G.5 claim arms, B.3 rank 14 (checkpoint rule as a sweepable choice), C.4 evergreen ('refreshed baseline arms')
findings.problem: Arm matching checks transitions, torque, code identity and backend, but not config identity outside the arm-defining keys. A claim can compare SMAT with observation normalisation on against B2 with it off, or arms with different checkpoint rules (registry rank 14), different E or different evaluation seeds, and every C.10 check passes. The evergreen generator refreshes baseline arms after a code change, but not the SMAT arm of the same block.
findings.scenario: The user edits SMAT to v2 (normaliser frozen at stage end), leaves B0 at v1, and registers the comparison. Budgets and code identity match, and the normaliser difference is counted as part of the 'torque effect'.
findings.fix: C.10, add: 'Arms of a claim must share every registry choice except the keys the claim declares as arm-defining; the checkpoint rule, the evaluation episode count E and the evaluation seed list must be identical across arms. Refreshing any arm of a block re-runs all arms of that block.' G.5: the claim schema stores the arm-defining keys.
findings.test: Synthetic ledgers: a claim whose arms differ in an undeclared key, in checkpoint rule or in E is 'not comparable'; an evergreen refresh of B0 alone is refused.

findings.where: Part G.0 ('fixed before the evidence'), G.8 (GATE_HASH, epochs), C.14 (paper package); the repository is private
findings.problem: The value of the design rests on bands and rules fixed before the evidence, but the only proof is a hash chain in a private repository whose commit dates the authors control. A reviewer cannot check that criteria.yaml, check_gate.py and campaign.yaml existed before the first Stage-4 result.
findings.scenario: A reviewer asks how the tolerances can be shown to predate the results, and the answer is a private git log.
findings.fix: G.8, add: 'Before the first Stage-4 job, publish gate/criteria.yaml, gate/check_gate.py, eval/core, the claim templates and campaign.yaml to a timestamped public registry (an OSF preregistration or a Zenodo DOI), and record the DOI in ledger/epochs.jsonl. Every later gate or eval epoch is published the same way before any claim uses it.' C.14: the paper cites these DOIs.
findings.test: The runner refuses to start the first S4 job unless epochs.jsonl holds a registry DOI for the current GATE_HASH and EVAL_HASH; the doctor checks that each epoch has one.

findings.where: Part G.6 G5
findings.problem: G5 asks a second machine to reproduce 'the central cell on 3 seeds within the claim's band'. That re-runs the L3 conjunction, which a true effect passes only about 40–70 % of the time at n = 3 (RD-01), and retraining on another machine is not bitwise reproducible (different CPU kernels, SM-14), so G5 often fails correct claims. 'Within its interval' for the fresh-clone check is also undefined.
findings.scenario: A correct L3 claim fails G5 because one of the three Vast seeds has a negative-power fraction of 15.4 %.
findings.fix: G5: '(i) A fresh clone re-evaluates the stored checkpoints on the lab with bit-for-bit equal metrics. (ii) A second machine retrains the claim's primary contrast on 3 fresh blocks, and its mean lies inside the original claim's 95 % prediction interval for a mean of 3 (mean ± t·s·√(1/3 + 1/n)).'
findings.test: Synthetic replication rows drawn from the claim's own distribution pass at least 90 % of the time; rows shifted by 2 standard deviations fail at least 80 % of the time.

findings.where: Part C.10 'Suspicious results'
findings.problem: The suspect thresholds ignore the arm. B1 (u = u*(ω̂), with the sign of ω except where ω crosses zero within a step) should have a negative-power fraction near 1–3 %, so its rows will often be flagged below 1 %. B0 with the ×15 effort weight may exceed a 40 % reduction if the S2 baseline is saturated. Each flag needs a fresh seed and a clip before the row counts, which delays the controls for physically expected values.
findings.scenario: Every B1 row is flagged 'looks too good' and needs extra seeds, and the mechanism path waits on them.
findings.fix: C.10: 'Suspect thresholds depend on the arm kind. For a fixed law, compare the negative-power fraction with the value predicted by applying the law to the arm's own recorded hip velocity, and flag a difference of more than 5 points. For B0 the activation flag is above 60 %. The generic thresholds apply to learned arms.'
findings.test: A synthetic B1 row with a 0.8 % negative-power fraction that matches its prediction is not flagged; a SMAT row at 0.8 % is flagged.

findings.where: Part G.2 L1 (toe-off 55–61 %, reference plausibility: r ≥ 0.80 and ROM within ±30 %); G.3 symmetry r
findings.problem: The toe-off band's upper limit (61 %) excludes the common overground value of about 60–62 %, so a more physiological reconstruction can fail L1 (this norm was not re-checked here). The ±30 % ROM floor is labelled ours but has no stated basis. Because the positive controls require L0–L2, failing an 'ours' criterion blocks every negative verdict. Pearson r ignores amplitude and the ROM floor is checked per side, so a limp with +25 % ROM on one side and −25 % on the other passes both.
findings.scenario: The reconstruction has toe-off at 61.6 % on both sides and fails L1, so no Stage-4 verdict is ever allowed.
findings.fix: L1: 'Split into L1-published (symmetry, toe-off, speed, falls), which gates reproduction, and L1-plausibility (reference r ≥ 0.80, ROM within ±30 %, left/right ROM difference ≤ 15 % of the mean), which gates the words normal gait and is always reported. Toe-off band 55–62 %, with the source of the norm cited in criteria.yaml.'
findings.test: A synthetic seed with toe-off at 61.6 % passes L1-published; a seed with a ±25 % left/right ROM split fails L1-plausibility.

findings.where: Part G.3 and C.9 (deterministic actions, E episodes of 12 s, first 2 s discarded); myoassist_facts deterministic_eval
findings.problem: Deterministic evaluation matches MyoAssist's evaluator and is a reasonable primary. But S2 (entropy 0.001) and S4 (entropy 0.003) policies may carry different noise levels, and with a log-std init of 0.0 the deterministic mean can walk differently from the trained stochastic behaviour, which shifts activation levels in the two arms by different amounts. Nothing shows that 2 s removes the transient after a reset with activations set to zero.
findings.scenario: The four-group reduction is 10 % with deterministic actions and 4 % with sampled actions. Only the first is reported, and a reviewer asks which one training optimised.
findings.fix: G.3: 'A stochastic evaluation (sampled actions, same seeds) is a pre-registered sensitivity for every L3 and mechanism number and must agree in direction. Stationarity check: metrics from seconds 2–7 and 7–12 must agree within the noise floor, otherwise the discarded window grows to 4 s for all arms.'
findings.test: Synthetic rollouts with a 3 s transient trigger the longer window; an L3 card without the stochastic sensitivity is refused.

findings.where: Part G.7 benchmark path ('rankings ... are stable'); G.2 L3 A1 ('evaluated at 6 and at 25 Nm'); B.6 B4 ('scaled to SMAT's peak and RMS torque'); G.2 L4(a) ('no more than 5 % higher'); G.3 gait events (body weight)
findings.problem: Several quantities check_gate.py must compute are undefined. 'Stable rankings' has no statistic or threshold. A1's criterion does not say whether it is judged at 6 or at 25 Nm. Scaling B4 to both SMAT's peak and its RMS torque gives one free parameter two targets. 'No more than 5 % higher' RMS torque and positive work is not stated as a point estimate or a bound. The 5 % body-weight event threshold does not say whether body weight includes the device (78.09 kg or 82.99 kg).
findings.scenario: Codex picks a Kendall τ threshold after seeing the backends' rankings, and the benchmark path passes on a threshold chosen with the data in view.
findings.fix: In criteria.yaml, declare now: 'Benchmark stability: Kendall's W ≥ 0.7 across seeds, and every pairwise ordering significant on the CPU (Holm) keeps its sign on the GPU. A1 is judged at 6 Nm, and 25 Nm is reported. B4 matches SMAT's positive work, with peak and RMS reported. L4(a) torque: the one-sided 95 % upper bound of the paired ratio minus 1 is ≤ 5 %. Gait events use the stage's total model weight, device included.'
findings.test: Each quantity has a synthetic-ledger test with one passing case and one failing case, and check_gate.py raises on any criteria key without a declared statistic.

strengths: The gate is a pure function of a hash-chained ledger, frozen before the first result, and each single violation is tested alone. That is the right architecture for a reproduction whose value is its honesty.

The corrected readings of the papers (left-right symmetry, Stage-2-versus-Stage-1 RMSE, the confounded 10.1 %) and the reward algebra (the u = ω̂ optimum, the LQ filter, bang-bang Stage 3) are right, and G.1 says plainly that the peak and negative-power gates test fidelity, not mechanism.

B0, the reward-matched zero-torque control, and A4, the proper minus-r_exo4 ablation, are the decisive missing experiments, and the design makes them first-class paired arms. B6 gives reviewers a published controller to compare with, and B7 is correctly labelled an oracle.
Pairing at the Stage-2 checkpoint, paired blocks released together, equal budgets and explicit 'not comparable' labels are the right defaults for every contrast.

The reported checkpoint is the final one by default and is never chosen by the reported metric; failed seeds stay in the pool; post-hoc seeds are reported but never gate; and the evergreen queue never adds seeds beyond a claim's pre-registered top-ups, which blocks open-ended optional stopping.
Every reported number is measured on CPU reference physics, and GPU trust rests on statistical and learning parity rather than on trajectory parity, which the probe shows is impossible with contacts.

Positive controls are required before any 'does not reproduce' verdict (the Luo-Collins lesson), and a clean negative with an open implementation counts as a paper, so the programme can converge in either direction.

The design is aware of the winner's curse: fresh-seed re-runs of sweep winners, tier calibration, an evaluation noise floor, a 'too close to call' rule, and a selection rule registered before every sweep.

One pre-declared primary activation metric (the four-group reduction) gates and the six-group value is reported, which avoids the union that the request's 'or' would create; activation is taken from data.act rather than the excitation, and bifemsh is excluded from hamstrings, with a sensitivity analysis.

Phase 2 gates the human before any device work (a replication gate, with no strength or shortening-velocity changes), counts incomplete runs as failures, and reports the force-velocity-relaxed diagnostic as the share of the model's own deficit that the device recovers.
